about: The files the self-host build of @requestport/web copies as they are, which no module of a chunk records (Plan 13, H.7 round 6; ruling 198 item 2). scripts/pack-requestport.mjs's verbatimPackages finds each file the build emits that is, byte for byte, a file of a package of apps/web's production closure, and keys it here by its SHA-256: an entry names the package that ships it (holder) and its path there, and what the file bundles, each with the licence its package.json declares and the text of its licence file, which THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES enters as bundled in the holder. A file so copied whose SHA-256 no entry names, an entry whose holder or path is not the file's, and an entry no file of the build matches each refuse the pack, so a changed file is reviewed here before it ships. Each bundled text is the licence file of that version's npm tarball (the tarball its entry's from names by its sha512), its trailing white space dropped. scripts/pack-requestport.test.mjs holds each entry's file against its holder's as apps/web installs it, and each bundled text against a SHA-256 that case pins, and against the store's copy where this tree installs that version. That release/licence-texts.json classifies each text was measured once, at H.7 round 6 (track-h.md); no test holds it.

files.reviewed: H.7 round 6, 2026-10-11, at next 16.3.8; re-reviewed at next 16.4.2 on 2026-10-23 (ruling 247), where it is byte for byte 16.3.8's, at the same SHA-256. Next's webpack configuration copies it as the polyfills chunk (16.4.2's dist/build/webpack-config.js:1758-1759, filePath require.resolve('./polyfills/polyfill-nomodule')). It is byte for byte @next/polyfill-nomodule@16.4.2's dist/polyfill-nomodule.js (its npm tarball, sha512-ZnxNPp7aGB3pidiykISLemAOoqRSL5o0FFlAs8F+MmnNITy2Gph+YvQqTE0blbV8DB9/IFocjSvXwksNy/Wkzg==), as it was 16.3.8's (sha512-JYUtE8qRJ+C04LWGqna6ltOSv4VmASEu2R/5ONUKoXzYJ6LwBeL+hrXIcwrLQU9F+jybksrUP3mDJOUp1IV9vg==), whose package.json scripts and dependencies and src/ 16.4.2's repeats: microbundle's IIFE build ('microbundle -i src/index.js -o dist/polyfill-nomodule.js -f iife --no-sourcemap --external none --no-pkg-main') of its src/index.js, which imports 56 core-js modules, whatwg-fetch and object-assign: the three packages its package.json pins beside microbundle (core-js 3.38.1, whatwg-fetch 3.0.0, object-assign 4.1.1). Read in the file: core-js's own version record (version "3.38.1", its copyright), whatwg-fetch's _bodyInit (8 times), 'Network request failed' and fetch's polyfill flag, and object-assign's 'Object.assign cannot be called with null or undefined'. The file carries no licence comment and no source map. The rest of it is @next/polyfill-nomodule's own two lines (Next's, under next's licence) and the bundler's module wrapper.

files.reviewed: H.7 round 6, 2026-10-11, at next 16.3.8; re-reviewed at next 16.4.2 on 2026-10-23 (ruling 247): the bundle analyser's copy is under the build id 16.4.2 ships (16.3.8's was WF5Ql9w6rALUjSQk9e-fZ), at the same SHA-256, and writeClientSsgManifest is 16.3.8's function. Next writes static/<build id>/_ssgManifest.js (dist/build/index.js's writeClientSsgManifest), naming the build's statically generated pages: for a build with none, two statements of its own, 'self.__SSG_MANIFEST=new Set([]);self.__SSG_MANIFEST_CB&&self.__SSG_MANIFEST_CB()'. That is byte for byte the bundle analyser's copy next ships, so it matches a file of next; it is Next's code, not a copy of another package's, and bundles nothing.
